summary.name: iPic
summary.one_liner: iPic is a macOS menu bar app that uploads images and files to image hosts and copies the resulting HTTP or Markdown links.
keywords: lossy image compression jpg png gif
use_cases: Uploading images to a cloud host and pasting the link into Markdown documents
Bulk uploading images from Finder via right-click or Command+U
Uploading screenshots or copied images from the clipboard
Compressing images before upload to save storage and bandwidth
Moving existing Markdown image links to a different image host
summary.what_it_does: iPic runs in the macOS menu bar and uploads images through drag and drop onto its icon, Finder Services (right-click or Command+U), or copied images from the pasteboard (Command+Shift+U). It can also upload images from other apps. Optional lossy compression is available for jpg, png and gif before upload. Uploaded links can be copied as plain HTTP links or Markdown links, and the app keeps the last 15 uploads in a history menu. The iPic Mover feature moves Markdown-linked images to a chosen image host in one click. The page lists default, Imgur, Flickr, Amazon S3, Qiniu, UpYun, Aliyun OSS and Tencent COS as supported hosts.
notable: Drag images onto the menu bar icon or use Finder Services with Command+U to upload
Switches between HTTP and Markdown link output and keeps a history of the last 15 uploads
iPic Mover moves Markdown-linked images to another image host in one click
Listed in awesome-mac under Other Tools as freeware
caveats: Only the default image host is free; other hosts (Imgur, Flickr, S3, etc.) require the paid iPic Pro subscription
Finder Services entry may take minutes or hours to appear after install unless the pbs refresh command is run
